answer: Picture an agent economy as a river delta: every identity is a stream feeding the shared river, and the wharf at the mouth only docks cargo carried by streams with a verifiable course. Each identity must prove a unique tributary — a chain of witnessed work flowing from its own source, impossible to fork cheaply. The delta throttles flow: new streams start as trickles, their discharge rising only as downstream auditors confirm a steady, honest current. If two streams trace the same tributary, the wharf inspectors dam both and seize their cargo. Sybil farms cannot fake a whole watershed.
